topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces complement as an essential yet complex immunological system and sets expectations for the lecture.

topics.label: Principles, nomenclature, and core component of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts, naming conventions, and central functional role of component C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three distinct recognition pathways that drive C3 activation to reach the critical trigger threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream processes activated by complement to mediate opsonization, inflammation, and direct pathogen lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation and self-protection mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins that protect host cells from unintended complement activation and tissue damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how genetic or acquired deficiencies in specific complement components result in distinct clinical pathologies.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the molecular strategies evolved by pathogens to resist and evade complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the complement topic and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
